A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIM bounds and Hutchinson estimator research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagonal-FIM computations for DistilBERT on AG News in Section 4.4 and Figure 1, and on SST-2 in Appendix O and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 reports original estimation errors and computational speed comparisons across six model-task combinations in Table 2, plus ground-truth FIM distributions in Figures 1–2 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The main Hutchinson estimator is retained. v2 Section 4.4 extends the optional rank-one core approximation to top-k eigenpairs, while Appendix B adds an equivalent square-root implementation without detach(). The extension has a specification ambiguity: Equation (8) uses xi_x although the text specifies k probes per example.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates AG News topic classification and SST-2 sentiment classification. v2 removes AG News, retains SST-2, and adds DBpedia ontology classification, MNLI natural language inference, CIFAR-100 image classification, and SpeechCommands audio classification. Coverage expands substantially beyond the original text-classification tasks.

E2.justification: The empirical FIM, unbiased Hutchinson, diagonal-core, and rank-one estimators remain evaluated. v2 Table 2 adds the rank-two variant, including in the retained SST-2 comparison. Monte Carlo estimation was not an evaluated comparator in v1, so its explicit exclusion in v2 is not a baseline removal.

E3.justification: v1 uses the first 128 examples for illustrative estimator distributions. v2 uses a fixed random subset of 128 batches of 64 examples, computes the exact diagonal FIM, and evaluates RelMAE with epsilon 10^-12 and relative computational speed. Its single-backward-pass-per-batch comparison introduces a substantially different evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted rank-one versus rank-two comparison in Table 2 and an informal numerical comparison of the original and square-root formulations in Appendix B. Existing layerwise diagnostics are revised to examine exact FIM distributions, including zero masses and differences between model components.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly averages 10 Hutchinson samples for variance reduction. v2 describes independent minibatch probes and accumulation under a single-backward-pass-per-batch budget. This changes stochastic aggregation, without establishing additional repeated experimental runs. Neither version reports seeds or between-run confidence intervals; analytical variance guarantees are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: The original approximation-density results are replaced by ground-truth histograms and quantitative error/speed comparisons. For example, v2 Table 2 reports Hutchinson versus empirical-FIM RelMAE of 0.18 versus 1.15 on SST-2 and 0.17 versus 56.8 on SpeechCommands. These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 Propositions 5 and 8 extend v1 Propositions 6 and 9 from rank one to rank k, with corresponding proof revisions in Appendices J and M. Lemma 2 adds an interior condition, and Section 4.2 adds minibatch variance reasoning under approximately equal batch contributions. The original spectral and estimator-variance results otherwise remain, sometimes relocated.

C1.justification: The central claims about deterministic FIM bounds and efficient unbiased estimation with bounded relative variability remain. v2 explicitly promotes an empirical study demonstrating production-setting advantages as a contribution. Its conclusion additionally claims straightforward integration into libraries for FIM or Hessian evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 adds practical estimator-selection guidance based on the new accuracy comparisons, qualifies power iteration by spectral-gap-dependent convergence, and explains the locality assumption behind moving averages. Appendix B discusses numerical stability of the square-root formulation. The absence of downstream optimizer development was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: Hardware changes from an Apple M1 laptop with 16 GB RAM to Nvidia H100 SXM5 GPUs. v2 specifies an actual 30-iteration power-method budget and gives log_softmax implementation guidance; v1 only suggested 10 iterations as an example. Conversely, v1's explicit DistilBERT checkpoint identifiers are omitted in v2.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially broadens positioning through pruning, transfer learning, fine-tuning, catastrophic forgetting, and foundational information geometry, with corresponding new citations. Section 3 newly contrasts the proposed bounds with monotonicity and coarse-graining bounds. The Sun–Nielsen preprint-to-publication update represents the same work, not an added research connection.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around motivation and explicit contributions. Estimator construction moves from the introduction into Section 4.2; core-space variance material and two estimator propositions move into appendices. Empirical and Monte Carlo FIM notation is separated, and the experimental narrative is substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: Both original estimator-by-layer density grids are replaced by grouped ground-truth histograms across models, with logarithmic horizontal axes, explicit zero masses, parameter counts, and median/95th-percentile markers. v2 adds the accuracy-and-speed Table 2 and revises the notation table. These are substantial display changes.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly visualizes approximations without measuring their errors against an exact reference. v2 Section 4.5 and Table 2 resolve this important evidential weakness through exact diagonal-FIM accuracy and computational-speed comparisons across text, vision, and audio. Clearer notation and organization also help. The new rank-k formula's probe-index ambiguity limits confidence in that extension, but does not outweigh the substantially stronger validation of the retained main estimator.
